examples.knowledge_point: Determining an Angular Rate Given a Related Rate
examples.problem: Given that $r=\sin\theta$ for $\theta = \theta(t),$ and that $\dfrac{\textrm d r}{\textrm d t}=\sqrt{2}$ at the point where $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4},$ find $\dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d r}{\textrm d t}=\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4},$ and solve for $\dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \sqrt{2} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\ \sqrt{2} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Given that $y=3{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}$ for $x=x(t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=3$ at the point where $x=-1,$ find $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (12{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=3$ and $x=-1,$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (12(-1)^{3}+6(-1)^{2}) \\ 3 & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (-6) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
